To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
an electric field applied in the direction perpendicular to the plane of the crystal surface induces anomalies in the reflection of electromagnetic waves from the surface of the crystal.
an external electric field can cause a change in the Goos– Hanchen effect in a ferromagnet.
an external electric field can change the magnitude and sign (i.e., the direction of shift) of the Goos-Hanchen effect.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of a constant electric bias on the reflection of an s-type electromagnetic beam, reflected from a ferromagnet.
the influence of the electric field on the optical properties of ferromagnets and ferromagnetic–nonmagnetic photonic crystals.
the effect of an external electric field on the reflection of an incident electromagnetic wave from a magnetized ferromagnet, and the effect this has on the Goos– Hanchen effect.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the anomalies in the reflection of the wave from the surface, and the change in the sign of the shift in the reflected beam, are due to the presence of an external electric field.
the external electric field can be used as an effective means for controlling the Goos– Hanchen shift in the reflection of light from the surface of ferromagnets.

the anomalies in the reflection of TE electromagnetic waves are caused by the presence of a constant electric-field-induced surface magnetic anisotropy, which leads to a shift in the position of the resonance in the reflection spectrum.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the external electric field can induce the anomalous behavior of the Goos-Hanchen effect in the ferromagnet–dielectric system.
the anomalies in the reflection coefficient of a ferromagnetic material in a constant external field lead to a change in the sign and magnitude of the Goos-Hanchen effect.
an external electric field can be used to control the reflection of a wave from a ferromagnet.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, in the case of a ferromagnetic material, the electric field can change the sign of the Goös–Hanchen shift, which, in the case considered, is a consequence of the fact that the reflection coefficient of the TE wave from the surface changes the sign of the external electric field.
the effect the external electric field has on the reflection of an incident TE plane wave from a ferromagnet can be used to control the Goos– Hanchen effect.
, in the presence of an external electric field, the Goos– Hanchen shift of a beam of plane waves reflected from a ferromagnet can be both positive and negative.
